f1.subset_rule: per (family, band) cell, in the fixed order of FAMILIES x BANDS: one stratum of the cell drawn from the l2_subset stream of the sealed seed, then 2 of its judged layouts without replacement; written to plan_frozen.json before any solve. Levels 0 and 2 are solved at both loads (level 1 is the judged solve). Level-1 error = |v1 - v2| + mfos.metrics.gci_step_floor(v0, v1, v2, 0.01 K); die averages <= 1 % of the level-1 die-local rise; spreads and same-stratum pair differences (hottest die by the level-1 die average, held fixed across levels) <= 0.1 K, and |v1 - v2| <= 0.1 K

bound.statement: one-sided 97 % bounds (Woodruff quantile bound, delete-one-layout jackknife, t(K-1), outward rounding) for A1-A4 and K1-K3; under the max over the two loads the upper bound is the max of the per-load upper bounds and the K1/K2 lower bound is the max of per-load lower bounds at 98.5 % (Bonferroni); A4/K3 by the Bonferroni quotient. More conservative than O002's 'upper 95 % bound' for passes and kills (a somewhat higher chance of INCONCLUSIVE): accepted by the founder, D0025 decision 1. Power (f3_simulation.json, D0025 context): at 0.6 x each threshold, joint power under t3 errors is 0.748 / 0.898 / 0.958 at m = 16 / 20 / 24; the 0.898 is really the power of A1, A2 and A4, since A3's power is 1.0 in that scenario (review T0420 (4)). For the L1 as measured on development rows (A4 = 0.366), joint power at m = 20 is 0.531 under t3 and 0.967 under normal errors, A4 alone driving the shortfall (T0434; simulated at m = 20 only). The two figures are different scenarios. m was resolved only on the grid {12, 16, 20, 24, 32}: an m between 16 and 20 needs a fresh simulation (review T0420 (5))
bound.decision: D0025 decision 1 (founder, 2026-11-17T01:26:21+00:00): CISpec(scheme='woodruff', level=0.94, cluster='layout'); the bound is mfos.metrics.quantile_ci (patch route I0211, merged on main in da2118fc). Every recompute entry except l1_eval_s_p50 carries this ci, as the row contract says

cfg.per_stratum_rule: fixed before the run (F3, review T0420 (3)): A2 per (family, dies) stratum (statistic: max over loads of the p95 of |Tj,avg,L1 - Tj,avg,ref| / die-local rise over the stratum's dies; bound: the same V4 Woodruff bound on the stratum's rows, layouts as units); A4 per die-count band 2-3 and 4-6 (statistic: A4's ratio on the band's switch rows at P_ref; bound: V4 ratio bound). Reported, not gated. With 32 layouts per stratum the per-stratum A2 upper bound is expected to sit at the stratum maximum or at +inf (q + t(31) se of the share near 1; review T0436; t(19) at the former m = 20): reports.json gives each stratum's point, bound, maximum and an upper_informative flag, and the counts of infinite and informative upper bounds; a per-stratum bound is never read as precise

f7.rule: per (family, band) cell: the pools' strata drawn from the f7_strata stream without replacement (2-3 band: both strata; 4-6: two of three); per pool, draws_per_pool layouts from its own f7 stream at the stratum's die size; the optimised layout is the draw with the lowest L1 hottest-die average (max over dies of L1's die average) at P_ref, ties to the lowest index. Solved by the reference at the judged level at both loads; its A1-type errors against every random judged layout of the same stratum reported (p95 and max per pool and load), not gated

isolated_die.definition: T_bp(all dies) + [box_series(die alone on the five substrate layers, laterally uniform over the baseplate, constant k at 363.15 K) - (T_c + P_i / (h A))] + P_i (t_attach / k_attach + t_die / k_die) / A_die: no inter-die coupling (solvers.thermal_series, Muzychka et al. 2003 / Carslaw and Jaeger 1959 Sec. 3.6)

nulls.die_position: per (family, dies, load, switch, die_index): mean reference die average of the other layouts of the stratum (leave-one-layout-out)
nulls.stratum_mean: die averages: per (family, dies, load, switch) the mean reference die average over every die of that switch in the other layouts; spreads: spread_null_K, the mean reference spread of the other layouts per (family, dies, load, switch); both leave-one-layout-out
nulls.applies: every null is computed at both loads. null_baselines applies each of the three nulls to A1 (dtj_pair_err_p95_K_max_load) and A4 (switch_spread_err_ratio_vs_stratum_mean) only, so mfos's evaluator marks A1 or A4 non_discriminating if a null meets it at its bound. A2 and A3 are not in applies_to: O002 F2 requires each null to fail A1 and the spread nulls to fail A4, and nothing else; the hypothesis says A3 (and A5) are each met by a layout-ignorant predictor on their own and that A1 and A4 separate L1 from the nulls; the A3 description says a stratum-mean spread may meet A3 alone. Development data agree (research/notes/o002-l1-design.md null table: stratum_mean and die_position A3-type 0.411 / 0.193 K, under A3's 1 K), so applying the nulls to A3 would make E007 unable to PASS (review T0436, the blocker of attempt 1). All three nulls predict spreads (null (c) max - min of its per-index means, null (a) its per-die isolated values), so all three are applied to A4. The gated sanity check f2_null_discrimination applies F2's point rule at P_ref on the judged rows. A2 and A3 of every null are reported (A2 also per stratum); the die-position null's A4 is close to the stratum-mean null's by construction (a max of leave-one-out means is at most the mean of maxima; equal when the same die indices are hottest and coldest in every layout; review T0435)

l1.timing: A5 = median wall time of L1.evaluate per (layout, load) over the 960 judged evaluations (32 x 15 strata x 2 loads), in one subprocess with OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/VECLIB/NUMEXPR thread variables = 1, after every P_ref calibration solve (level 0, development layouts) has finished and before any judged reference solve, with no solve running, in the sealed timing order, after one uncounted warm-up evaluation on a P_ref development layout. Every other L1 evaluation of the run (F4 constant-k ablation, F7 pools, F7 optimised layouts at half load) follows in the same process, untimed for A5. Host (reviews T0449/T0450 (5)) - A5 is timed on the host that runs the registered run's L1 phase, fixed here as the burst VM of compute option A (config.compute.vm.machine, the policy's route; the L1 phase records node, platform and processor in l1_phase.json and the run's domain records cpu). If the founder chooses option B, the host of the L1 phase is fixed in that decision before registration. T0398's development A5 was timed on the founder's Mac (Apple silicon), a development figure, not the registered host

Recomputed from experiments/drafts/E007.dev_rows.json meta.reference_cpu_wall (T0398's 90 level-1 solves): max 4.32 kB/DOF with base RSS (0.3 GB) excluded, 4.98 kB/DOF with it included (both side_by_side_2_j02 half_P_ref, 2.27 GB at 0.455 M DOF); T0456's 36 level-1 solves 4.33 / 4.99 kB/DOF. The earlier source text's 4.29 kB/DOF was neither of these. On all 126 measured level-1 solves the admission estimate is 1.15 to 2.24 x the measured peak RSS (never below it; 1.82 is the maximum over T0398's 90 solves, 2.24 over T0456's 36; review T0465).
